lessons: Ripe beats unripe: stripping unripe apples pays little and leaves the patch bare. Wait near a patch and eat apples at ripe stage when possible.
Once a patch is fully eaten (0 apples around) it NEVER regrows; with 1-2 left regrowth is very slow. So do not strip a patch bare — leave 2-3 apples hanging to keep regrowth alive.
Stun (zap) works: a 12-step stun window let me take contested ripes. Worth it when a rival sits on the only good patch.
C competes hard on yellows, D and E on purples. Rivals eat unripe and over-ripe too, so apples I plan to ripen may vanish — check who is near before waiting on a patch.
Patches are small and get bared fast with 5 agents; late-trial play is mostly exploring unseen ground. Learn patch locations early, visit in an order that leaves regrowth sources intact.
Skipping stages rivals avoid (e.g. over-ripe) got me apples when contested, but over-ripes rot — eat them before they vanish.
Purple patch rows 4-5 cols 10-12 and rows 12-14 cols 18-20, yellow rows 4-8 cols 17-21, green rows 11-12 cols 12-14, purple rows 8-12 cols 6-8 — all known patches went bare by t102.
todo: Trial 2: map more patches early (explore edges/unseen ground) instead of over-working the first patches.
Leave 2-3 apples per patch as regrowth seeders; revisit later for the regrown ripes.
Learn payoffs of colours/stages I have not eaten (green, red, cyan, over-ripe/yellow stages).
Use zaps on rivals who monopolise the best ripe patch, then eat during their 12-step stun.
